lesson_title: What Is in Your School Bag?
hook_text: A pencil, an apple, a phone and a pair of shoes. How many countries are in your school bag?
clip_script: Soweto, one school bag tipped onto a desk. An apple from the Western Cape. A calculator made in Asia. Shoes put together from leather, rubber and glue from different places. A cooldrink from a factory in Gauteng. Every item reached us through trade, the buying and selling of goods and services. Producers make things, consumers use them, and markets bring them together. Trade links our street to the whole world.
visual_style: Whiteboard school bag emptying, each item drawing an arrow back to a dot on a map of South Africa or the world.
mood: Curious and surprising, like discovering a hidden journey.
pacing: Quick tip of the bag, one item at a time with its arrow, ending on a map full of arrows.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and check the labels on five things at home to see where they were made.
